L4·N10764unmasked layer
Fires on word-internal continuation fragments — sub-word pieces that complete a longer/compound or numeric-abbreviated expression (e.g. "grav" in "aggravated", "reg" in "Fabreguettes", "x" in a phone extension, "4" in "24/7", "-hour" in "60-hour"); notably, similar continuation pieces ("-way" in "half-way", "st" in "1st", "CS" in "NRCS") drive it strongly negative, so it is a surface-form/token-boundary detector rather than a semantic one.

L4·N10910unmasked layer
This neuron fires (weakly-to-moderately) on word-internal sub-word fragments that complete proper nouns/acronyms or compound words (the "HR" of NIHR, "us"+"cript" of Manuscript, "if" of Tardif, "man" of Grossman), and is most strongly *suppressed* by fragments of medical/Greek-Latin stems such as "Onc(ology)" and "ophthalm(ologist)" — i.e. it is a sub-token-identity detector rather than a semantic one.
